Exploratory QA report

localhost:4201/login

Target http://localhost:4201/login · Generated 2026-07-28T00:00:00Z · Browser playwright-mcp · Report v1.0

Login page QA — negative and edge handling is solid; double-submit and input hygiene need fixes; positive login is blocked pending user sign-in.

Issues found
0Critical
1High
2Medium
3Low
18Total
15Passed
2Failed
1Blocked
0Skipped

About this report

This is an exploratory QA report. An AI QA engineer opened the application in a real browser driven by Playwright, worked through 18 test cases, and captured proof for every defect it reports.

Each finding below says what happens today, what should happen instead, and how to see it for yourself — so nothing here has to be taken on trust.

What was tested

Check whether a first-time user can sign in to the admin console, and whether the login form behaves correctly when they get it wrong — bad password, unknown email, empty fields, pasted whitespace, and a slip of the mouse.

  • The sign-in form at /login: email field, password field, password visibility toggle, Login button, and the Forgot Password link
  • Every way a sign-in can fail: wrong password, unknown email, empty fields, malformed email, and text pasted with surrounding spaces
  • The GraphQL authentication request the page sends, and the error message it returns
  • Hostile input in both fields: SQL-injection strings and an XSS payload
  • The form on a 375px-wide mobile screen, and with the keyboard alone
  • What the browser downloads on a first, uncached visit to the page
Area checkedWhat that means
FunctionalityDoes the feature do what it is supposed to do, including when the input is wrong?
APIThe network requests the page makes — whether they are correct, and how the page handles a bad response
PerformanceHow much the page downloads and how quickly it becomes usable
Security (client-side)Client-side exposure only: where credentials and tokens are stored, what leaks into URLs and error messages
UILayout and visual states — empty, loading, error — including a narrow mobile screen
UXWhether the flow makes sense to a person using it, and whether the wording helps them

Not covered in this run

  • Signing in successfully. Doing so needs real credentials, which a QA run must never enter on the user's behalf — so everything behind the login wall is untested.
  • Password reset beyond confirming the link navigates: no email was sent or received.
  • Security headers. This run hit a local development server, where they are absent by design; they must be re-checked against the deployed environment.
  • Rate limiting and account lockout after repeated failures, which would have locked the test account.
  • Data was not examined — whether the numbers and text on screen match the system of record behind them
  • Could not be run: TC-1 (Valid credentials lead to a successful login and redirect)

How to read the findings

SeverityWhat it means
CriticalBlocks release. Data loss, a security hole, or a core flow that cannot be completed.
HighFix before release. A user hits this on a normal path and the product does the wrong thing.
MediumFix soon. Real but survivable — a workaround exists, or the path is less common.
LowWorth fixing. Polish, hygiene, or a measurement that needs confirming before it is acted on.

Findings

High

Double-click on Login fires two GraphQL auth requests

EXP-1
functional Confirmed
Current behaviour
Two identical POST requests are sent to https://admin.f2finterview.com/graphql for one submit. The button stays enabled while the first request is in flight.
Expected behaviour
One authentication request per submit. The Login button is disabled from the first click until the request settles.
Reproduction
  1. Open http://localhost:4201/login
  2. Enter a valid-format email and any password
  3. Double-click Login within ~300 ms
  4. Watch the Network panel
Fix direction
Disable the submit control on click and re-enable it in the request's finally/completion handler; ignore submits while a request is pending.
Medium

Password field uses autocomplete=new-password on a sign-in form

EXP-2
ux Confirmed
Current behaviour
The password input declares autocomplete="new-password", and the email input is type="text" with no autocomplete hint.
Expected behaviour
On a sign-in form the password input declares autocomplete="current-password" and the email input is type="email" autocomplete="username", so saved credentials are offered and mobile keyboards show the right layout.
Reproduction
  1. Open /login
  2. Inspect the email and password inputs in the DOM
Fix direction
Set autocomplete="current-password" on the password field; set type="email" autocomplete="username" on the email field.
Medium

No maximum length on email or password

EXP-3
security Confirmed
Current behaviour
Both values are accepted and sent to the API unchanged; the form shows no length validation.
Expected behaviour
Client-side maximum lengths (e.g. 254 for email per RFC 5321, a documented bound for password) reject over-long input before a request is made.
Reproduction
  1. Open /login
  2. Paste a 312-character email and a 502-character password
  3. Submit
Fix direction
Add maxlength attributes and matching form-control validators; mirror the bounds server-side so the client is not the only check.
Low

Leading and trailing spaces in the email are not trimmed

EXP-4
ux Confirmed
Current behaviour
The untrimmed value is validated and submitted, so a copy-paste with a trailing space reads as an invalid email.
Expected behaviour
The email is trimmed before validation and before the request, so surrounding whitespace does not change the outcome.
Reproduction
  1. Open /login
  2. Type " user@example.com " with surrounding spaces
  3. Submit
Fix direction
Trim the email on blur and again before submit; keep the raw value only for display.
Low

Both inputs share name="inputTxt"

EXP-5
ui Confirmed
Current behaviour
The email and password inputs both use name="inputTxt", so they are indistinguishable to password managers, autofill, and any test selecting by name.
Expected behaviour
Each input has a distinct, meaningful name (email, password) matching its autocomplete role.
Reproduction
  1. Open /login
  2. Inspect the name attribute on both inputs
Fix direction
Rename the inputs to email and password and update any bindings or selectors that relied on inputTxt.
Low

Development main.js is ~16 MB on a cold load

EXP-6
performance Partially reproduced
Current behaviour
main.js transfers at roughly 16 MB cold, because this is an unoptimised ng serve development build.
Expected behaviour
A production build ships a bundle an order of magnitude smaller; this figure is not a production measurement and must be re-measured against a built artifact.
Reproduction
  1. Hard-reload http://localhost:4201/login with an empty cache
  2. Read the transfer size of main.js in the Network panel
Fix direction
Re-measure against ng build --configuration production before treating bundle size as a defect; if it remains large, budget it in angular.json.

Data validation

Not in scope: no data-store access was provided for this run.

Suggested fix order

  1. EXP-1 — one auth request per submit (a duplicate login attempt is user-visible and can trip rate limiting)
  2. EXP-3 — bound the input lengths on both client and server
  3. EXP-2 — correct the autocomplete and input types so credential managers work
  4. EXP-5 — give the inputs distinct names
  5. EXP-4 — trim the email before validation
  6. EXP-6 — re-measure the bundle against a production build before acting

Recommendations

ActionPriority
Guard the submit handler against concurrent requests, then re-run TC-16high
Add maxlength bounds to both fields and mirror them server-sidemedium
Ask the user to sign in once so TC-1 (positive login) can be unblockedmedium
Re-check security headers against the deployed environment, not ng servelow

Verified working

  • Empty required fields keep Login disabled and show "This field is required"
  • An invalid email format shows "Please enter valid Email" and blocks submit
  • Wrong or unknown credentials stay on /login with an "Invalid login credentials" banner
  • The password visibility toggle switches the input between password and text
  • "Forgot Password?" navigates to /forgot-password
  • An XSS payload in the email field does not execute; it is treated as an invalid email
  • A SQLi-style password does not bypass authentication; the page stays on login with an error
  • The 375px mobile layout has no horizontal overflow and the form remains usable
